bib.title: FAIRSEQ: A Fast, Extensible Toolkit for Sequence Modeling

question: Can a PyTorch toolkit give researchers and practitioners fast, extensible distributed and mixed-precision training and inference for translation, summarization and language modeling?
contributions: A common interface across models and tasks extended with user-supplied plug-ins
Efficient distributed and mixed precision training over datasets with hundreds of millions of sentences
State-of-the-art implementations and pretrained models for machine translation, summarization and language modeling
Optimized inference with beam search, diverse beam search and top-k sampling

method.summary: FAIRSEQ is an open-source PyTorch sequence modeling toolkit with five plug-in types (models, criterions, tasks, optimizers, LR schedulers), synchronous multi-GPU training with overlapped gradient sync and gradient accumulation, FP16 compute with FP32 master updates and dynamic loss scaling, and incremental decoding. It is demonstrated on WMT En-De/En-Fr translation, WikiText-103 and One Billion Word language modeling, and CNN-DailyMail summarization.
method.task: sequence modeling toolkit: translation, language modeling, abstractive summarization

datasets.name: WMT'14 En-Fr
datasets.source: WMT'14, setup of Gehring et al. (2017)

datasets.name: CNN-DailyMail (full-text, no entity anonymization)
datasets.source: Hermann et al. 2015; Nallapati et al. 2016; See et al. 2017
datasets.preprocessing: articles truncated to 400 tokens; BPE with 30K operations

models.name: Transformer LM, adaptive inputs, WikiText-103
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer with adaptive input embeddings

models.name: Transformer LM, adaptive inputs, One Billion Word
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer with adaptive input embeddings

models.name: Summarization base Transformer encoder + decoder
models.architecture: base Transformer encoder-decoder; optional pretrained LM representations fed to encoder
models.init_from: optional LM trained on newscrawl and CNN-Dailymail

training.objective: cross-entropy implied; criterions are pluggable (also sequence-level losses, online backtranslation, mixture-of-experts EM)
training.optimizer: wrappers around most PyTorch optimizers plus Adafactor; specific optimizer per experiment not stated
training.lr_schedule: inverse square-root (Vaswani 2017) and cyclical warm-restart schedulers available; per experiment not stated
training.batch_size: translation results used a bigger batch size and increased learning rate than Vaswani et al. 2017; no values given
training.precision: FP16 forward/backward and gradient all-reduce, FP32 parameter updates, dynamic loss scaling
training.hardware: V100 GPUs; 8 GPU and 128 GPU runs
training.wall_clock: En-De ~12 h on 8 GPUs, ~1.3 h on 128 GPUs; En-Fr ~73 h on 8 GPUs, ~7.2 h on 128 GPUs

other.batching: source/target pairs grouped by similar length to minimise padding; mini-batch content fixed, order shuffled each epoch
other.multi_gpu: NCCL2 + torch.distributed, synchronous; gradient sync overlapped with backward in a background thread once a buffer reaches a threshold; gradient accumulation over several sub-batches per GPU
other.checkpoints: contain full model, optimizer and dataloader state

inference.decoding: beam search width 4, length penalty 0.6 for translation; summarization: tuned minimum output length, no repeated trigram; diverse beam search and top-k sampling also supported

other.incremental_decoding: caches states of generated tokens in each beam; up to an order of magnitude faster than naive
other.inference_batching: variable number of examples up to a user-specified token count

metrics.name: translation speed
metrics.definition: sentences/sec on WMT'14 En-De test, big Transformer, V100

eval.protocol: single reported numbers; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated

limits: System demo paper: no ablations of overlap sync or gradient accumulation; the only speed number is FP16 vs FP32 inference (Table 1).
Learning rates, batch sizes, optimizer, step counts, dropout and parameter counts are not given; reproduction relies on the code and Ott et al. 2018b.
Single runs, no variance reported. 2019 toolkit (LSTM, convolutional and Transformer seq2seq); predates large decoder-only pretraining.
